arguments.reason: external1->web1 and web1->external1 both fail with 100% loss while all other endpoint pairs succeed. leaf2 (gateway for web1) has no route for 203.0.113.0/24 beyond its directly-connected local route, and external1 has no route to 10.10.40.0/24 beyond its connected subnet. Adding a /32 route for external1 (203.0.113.10) toward the upstream gateway 203.0.113.254 restores the intended external reachability without touching the connected 203.0.113.0/24 segment.

steps.error: transaction has no complete rollback: every confirmed successful change requires rollback_commands

arguments.name: default
arguments.reason: Remove the default route just added (next-hop 203.0.113.254 does not exist; it did not restore external1<->web1 connectivity).

external1->web1 fails because external1 has no route for 10.10.40.0/24 (its default via 203.0.113.1 leads back to leaf2, a loop). Adding a static route via 203.0.113.1 (the gateway on the shared 203.0.113.0/24 segment) restores the intended external-to-DMZ path.

web1->external1 fails because web1 has no route for 203.0.113.0/24; its default via 10.10.40.1 reaches leaf2, but leaf2 must be told to forward toward the internet. Adding a static route via 10.10.40.1 (its gateway) restores the intended DMZ-to-external path.
Remove the static route added in the previous attempt; it did not restore external1->web1 connectivity.
Remove the static route added in the previous attempt; it did not restore web1->external1 connectivity.

Test: add an explicit /32 for external1 on the leaf2 gateway. If forwarding between directly-connected subnets is blocked, this should also fail; if only the /24 local route is the problem, this should restore web1->external1.
Remove the test /32; it did not restore web1->external1 connectivity, confirming the drop is policy, not routing.
